lines.before: **Theorem.** Suppose that a subgroup $G \subset \mathrm{GL}(n, \mathbb{R})$ acts simply transitively on $\mathcal{F}$ (that is, for any two flags $F_1$ and $F_2$ there exists a unique transformation $g \in G$ for which $g(F_1) = F_2$). Then $L$ can be given a Euclidean metric so that $G$ becomes the group of orthogonal transformations.
